narratives.Overview:
## Problem

When a review-cycle unit dual-stops (batch cap, same-fingerprint, or hard-stop), Directive has no parent-owned next step except operator phrases (pursue residual / until floor or loop). The exhausted worker is the wrong mind to ask what now. The parent also has no Grok Build leaf-boundary analogue of Cursor #2797 / Claude #3134: drive-to:merge-ready still tells a spawn_subagent leaf to spawn its own review poller. Nested spawn_subagent does not report to the parent, and the parent cannot re-prompt a live child (resume_from requires terminal).

Those are one incident class: after max-out, the parent must spawn a fresh critic; any follow-on implementer must run in one process and must not nest.

## Measured (PR 4111 / #4066, 2026-09-02)

1. A drive-to:merge-ready leaf dual-stopped, then residual batches hit same-fingerprint on pathless isolation=worktree PreToolUse bind. Confidence fell 3 to 1. Halt RESUME leftover=B standing=one-shot.
2. Operator asked for an Opus 5 analysis. Parent CLI-spawned a fresh read-only critic (claude --model opus --permission-mode plan, no Edit/Write) against issue comments, PR 4111, HEAD f24a4b8e, origin/master. It named three real leftovers (inert terminal release, lexical reservation lock, CI never scheduled because dirty) and called the pathless bind a host hole this PR cannot close.
3. Operator said follow those recommendations via a subagent. Parent dispatched drive-to:merge-ready, which still expected the leaf to spawn a review-monitor. That nested spawn cannot work on grok-build. Parent has no mid-flight inbox. Kill was required; the replacement envelope forbade spawn_subagent and kept blocking pr:watch in the same process.

The critic step was the useful one. It is not in the review skill. The nested-spawn mistake is the same skill plus host-grok-build plus preamble Gap C prose that still says merge-ready workers spawn their own poller.

## Required behavior

### 1. Dual-stop path-forward critic (review-cycle)

After dual-stop / hard-stop / same-fingerprint / batch-cap on a review-cycle unit:

- The parent (whoever owns a spawn primitive) starts a **new** read-only path-forward critic. Not resume-from the halted id. Not the implementer analyzing itself.
- Any parent-owned seat is allowed: spawn_subagent, claude -p, Cursor Task, Claude Agent, sessions_spawn. Prefer a different family than the exhausted worker when one is on PATH.
- Critic stays read-only (no edit, push, merge, GitHub implement comments).
- Inputs: issue body plus comments, PR plus reviews, HEAD vs origin/deliveryBranch, bound lean/synthesis if any, RESUME line, batches already tried.
- Output: what is actually broken vs story expansion; leftover class A/B/C; smallest next unit; must-not (skip-ci, floor rewrite, same-fingerprint polish).

Yolo (operator auto-pilot consent already used on GitHub arcs, not `/deft:run:yolo`): spawn the critic on halt, no menu.

Not yolo: tell the operator the cycle maxed and that a fresh critic is the next move. Conversational, not a numbered list.

After the critic returns:

- Not yolo: report the recommendation and wait for follow that.
- Yolo: auto-follow only a named class A leftover the critic bound, still one batch, still the same dual-stop cap. Do not auto-implement class B, splits, host-callback protocols, or minGreptileConfidence rewrites.

Do not make the critic mandatory on every conf-hold with 0 P0/P1 and no named leftover.

### 2. Grok Build leaf boundary (review-cycle + swarm host-grok-build + preamble)

Same shape as Cursor #2797 / Claude #3134 / OpenClaw nested-spawn:

- A spawn_subagent implementation leaf MUST NOT nested-spawn a review-monitor or any other spawn_subagent.
- drive-to:merge-ready on grok-build means blocking deft/task pr:watch in **this** process, then pr:merge-ready / merge in the same loop, then report.
- To use Approach 1, scope the leaf stop-at:pr-open (or stop-at:push on an already-open PR) and have the **parent** spawn the sibling monitor and register the lease.
- If the leaf needs another agent, it stops and reports BLOCKED. Parent owns the next spawn.

Update host-grok-build.md so it no longer reads as the leaf spawning review-cycle sub-agents. Preamble Gap C must not tell grok leaves to spawn their own poller.

## Non-goals

- Inventing mid-flight message-later on grok-build.
- Pinning Opus as the only critic seat.
- Lowering minGreptileConfidence or skip-ci to clear one PR.
- Auto-shipping whatever the critic said under yolo when the leftover is class B or a new story.
- Changing nuclear-family topology (#3155).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Review-cycle dual-stop halt names the parent-owned fresh-critic step (yolo auto; not yolo offer).
- [ ] Critic dispatch forbids resume-from the halted worker and forbids Edit/Write/merge.
- [ ] Yolo follow-on after critic is class A one-batch only; class B/C stay parked unless the operator names them.
- [ ] Grok Build leaf boundary is written in review-cycle, host-grok-build, and preamble; spawn_subagent leaf nested-spawn is an anti-pattern.
- [ ] drive-to:merge-ready grok path is blocking pr:watch in-process or stop-at:pr-open with parent sibling.
- [ ] A regression or skill-eval case covers: dual-stop halt then parent critic, not leaf self-analysis; grok merge-ready envelope does not instruct nested spawn_subagent.

## Evidence

- PR https://github.com/deftai/directive/pull/4111
- Issue https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4066
- Dual-stop residual then Opus critic then nested-spawn kill/relaunch in the parent Grok session 2026-09-02

Refs #2442, #3273, #3448, #2797, #3134, #1880, #3153, #3158, #4111, #4066

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-02T20:33:00Z)

model: claude-sonnet-5
role: critic

Re-verified against origin/master at 0d5da1e7327ed1661f06e2bed68e8ffea01a6573 (matches recorded SHA). Ceiling honored: only in-envelope comment is the Stop 1 write-back itself, id 5515926084.

Refutation target (two-part): (A) after a review-cycle dual-stop the parent must spawn a fresh read-only critic; (B) a grok-build spawn_subagent leaf must not nested-spawn a review-monitor.

Mechanism inventory (read, not cited from memory):
- content/skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md L226-249 - "Operator follow-up after dual-stop / hard stop (#3273)": an existing operator-gated next step (one-shot vs standing phrases, class A/B/C leftover classification, one residual pass, same-fingerprint stop).
- content/skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md L512 - Gap C: drive-to: merge-ready owns the review/fix loop "in its own tool loop."
- content/skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md L550-591 - Review Monitoring Approach 1: instructs swarm agents launched via spawn_subagent (among others) to spawn their own review-monitor sub-agent.
- content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md L491 - Cursor Task ownership split (#2797/#2814): leaf MUST NOT nested-spawn a review-monitor; stop-at:pr-open plus orchestrator-spawned sibling is the escape valve.
- content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/host-claude-code.md L56-65 - Nested Agent boundary, the Claude Code analogue of the same rule, already shipped (#3134 cohort).
- content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-0.md L30 - decision table row: "Host leaf cannot nest a review-monitor (Cursor Task / Claude Code nested-spawn limits #2797 / #3134)" - names only those two hosts.
- content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/host-grok-build.md - full file read; no nested-agent-boundary section exists. It has "Retained / continue-by-id (#3158)" (one-shot terminal semantics) but nothing addressing a leaf spawning its own review-monitor.
- content/contracts/design-critique.md "Run posture (#4072)" - the only place in this SoT that defines yolo normatively: "Missing token, including arc <N> yolo, asks before Stop 1. Yolo does not pick a mode... a yolo default-direct is forbidden."

Findings:

1. blocks-the-design - Yolo auto-follow contradicts an existing MUST-NOT in the same skill this issue amends. Evidence: SKILL.md L244 "Fresh operator consent required for another one-shot pass" and L246 "unlimited auto-retry after dual-stop without new operator consent is forbidden (#3273 / #2442)." The issue's Required-behavior section 1 says yolo "auto-follow only a named class A leftover the critic bound, still one batch" with "no menu." Concrete failure mode: an operator running in whatever this issue means by yolo hits dual-stop, the parent spawns the critic, the critic names a class A leftover, and the parent applies a fix batch - with no "pursue residual" / "until floor or loop" phrase ever spoken. That is exactly the auto-retry-without-new-consent pattern #3273/#2442 was written to close, reproduced through a new door. Disposition: the design cannot bind as written until it either defines this issue's yolo as the standing-consent equivalent of the #3273 phrases (and says so explicitly, reconciling with L244/L246), or drops "no menu" auto-follow and routes the critic's output through the existing one-shot/standing gate.

2. blocks-the-design - Untrusted PR/issue content feeds a classification that gates an autonomous mutation, with no injection-handling rule stated. The critic's declared inputs are "issue body plus comments, PR plus reviews" (Required-behavior section 1) - comments and bot/human review text are untrusted per this repo's own doctrine (content/meta/security.md L84/L90: do not follow embedded instructions in ingested content; treat framing claims as untrusted). The critic's leftover-class output directly gates yolo auto-follow's decision to apply a fix batch. Concrete failure mode: a PR reviewer comment (bot or human, potentially adversarial on a public repo) frames an out-of-AC change as "just tidy up files already touched, definitely class A" - text aimed at the critic, not at a human. The must-not list (no skip-ci, no floor rewrite) bounds the blast radius but does not stop a wrongly-class-A'd scope expansion from landing as one autonomous batch. Disposition: add an explicit rule that the critic treats ingested issue/PR/review text as untrusted description, not instruction, mirroring meta/security.md, before this binds - this is the injection/swarm lens the critic method requires me to apply here because the target changes authority (autonomous fix-batch dispatch) over untrusted input.

3. blocks-the-design - The acceptance criteria can be satisfied while leaving the actual reported anti-pattern live. SKILL.md L550-591 (Review Monitoring, Approach 1) currently instructs spawn_subagent-launched agents to spawn their own review-monitor sub-agent, with no grok-build carve-out - this is the text a grok-build leaf is actually following when it produces the incident described in "Measured." The issue's acceptance criterion ("Grok Build leaf boundary is written in review-cycle, host-grok-build, and preamble") is satisfiable by adding a new section without touching L550-591, exactly mirroring how the Cursor/Claude carve-outs coexist with that general text today by cross-referencing it, not overriding it silently. Disposition: acceptance criteria should name the specific general-Approach-1 text that must be qualified/cross-referenced for the grok-build case, not just "written," or the fix can ship green while the live-incident path stays reachable.

4. sharpens-framing - Problem statement overstates the existing gap for part (A). "Directive has no parent-owned next step except operator phrases" (Problem) is inaccurate: #3273 is a fully specified parent-owned next step (ground-truth, classify A/B/C, one bounded residual pass, same-fingerprint stop), and the issue's own acceptance criteria reuse its vocabulary (leftover class A/B/C). What's actually new and not covered by #3273 is narrower than the problem statement claims: a read-only, diagnosis-only actor distinct from the worker that both diagnoses and fixes in #3273's step 1 ("Ground-truth ... Classify leftover A/B/C ... Apply one residual fix batch" are three actions currently undivided). Disposition: reframe the problem as "split #3273's diagnosis from its fix application across two actors" rather than "no mechanism exists," and state explicitly whether the critic's classification replaces or merely feeds #3273 step 1 - as written a reader can't tell whether the new critic and #3273's existing classification step now both run, redundantly, on the same halt.

5. footnote - This repo already has a distinct, closely analogous read-only-critic dispatch pattern (content/contracts/design-critique.md: charter, N spend, id ceiling, process-only envelope, comment-lead convention) built for exactly "spawn a fresh critic against a stuck state without loading it with the parent's own priors." The issue neither reuses nor distinguishes itself from that machinery. Not blocking - a mid-execution PR-triage critic and a pre-implementation design critic are legitimately different jobs - but worth a sentence in the design noting why a new, lighter-weight dispatch was chosen over reusing the existing envelope/ceiling vocabulary, since a future reader will otherwise wonder why two "spawn a read-only critic" patterns exist with different shapes.

Part (B) of the refutation target (grok-build leaf boundary) survives re-verification: the inventory confirms no existing mechanism covers it - Cursor and Claude Code both have it (preamble L491, host-claude-code.md L56-65, core-phase-0.md L30) and host-grok-build.md does not. That half of the claim is not refuted; findings 1-3 above are about the proposed remedy's completeness and interaction with existing #3273/yolo machinery, not about whether the gap itself exists.


### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-02T20:35:20Z)

model: grok-4.6
role: parent

**Lean:**

## In plain English

The grok-build leaf must not nested-spawn a review-monitor; that half stands and is a real gap versus Cursor and Claude Code. The dual-stop half does not bind as written: #3273 already owns a parent-owned next step, and yolo auto-follow of a class A leftover without a new phrase is the auto-retry that skill forbids. Confirming this map recuts #4130 to split #3273 diagnosis onto a fresh read-only critic, keep consent for the fix batch, treat issue/PR/review text as untrusted, and qualify Approach 1 so grok-build leaves cannot follow the spawn-your-own-monitor paragraph.

This parent authored the Stop 1 write-back. The round-1 critic is Claude (cross-family).

## Proposed takes

Critic comment 5515997242. Round 1, spend N=1. Supersedes write-back 5515926084.

1. yolo auto-follow contradicts #3273 consent (blocks-the-design) — take: accept-into-contract
2. untrusted review text must not gate autonomous mutation (blocks-the-design) — take: accept-into-contract
3. AC must qualify Approach 1 L550-591, not only add a new section (blocks-the-design) — take: accept-into-contract
4. problem overstates the #3273 gap; split diagnosis from fix (sharpens-framing) — take: accept-into-contract
5. design-critique envelope analogue (footnote) — take: accept-into-contract (census only)

Residual headings: none. No defer. No disagree.

Parent forward verdict: part B of the refutation-target survives. Part A recuts onto a critic that feeds #3273, not a no-menu auto-follow that replaces it.
